ftm.office_official: Register of Wills for Anne Arundel County
ftm.office_address: 2011 E Commerce Park Drive, Annapolis, Maryland 21401
ftm.notes: The Register of Wills handles probate filings. Estate search is available online via the statewide portal. Walk-ins are accepted until 3:30 PM. Email is for general inquiries, not for filings or Public Information Act requests. Call before visiting to understand procedures and required documents.

ftm.data_type: Foreclosure (first public signal for this state's process)
ftm.office_official: Circuit Court for Anne Arundel County, Clerk of the Court
ftm.notes: Maryland uses either judicial or nonjudicial foreclosure. Judicial foreclosures are filed in the Circuit Court. The daily civil docket is updated between 3:00 and 3:30 PM each day for the next day's docket. Users should refresh their screen to ensure an up-to-date docket. Nonjudicial foreclosures would be recorded with the Land Records Department.

ftm.data_type: Recorder / Register of Deeds - Lien & Deed Index
ftm.office_official: Circuit Court for Anne Arundel County, Land Records Department
ftm.notes: The Land Records Department records deeds, mortgages/deeds of trust, releases, subdivision/condominium plats, and other real property instruments. Verified land records can be viewed online at mdlandrec.net (requires account with Maryland State Archives). Plats can be viewed at plats.msa.maryland.gov. The office is prohibited from providing legal assistance or title searches. Copies are $0.50 per page, certified copies are an additional $5.00 per document.

ftm.office_official: Anne Arundel County Office of Finance, Tax Sale Division
ftm.notes: The county holds an annual tax sale in June. The county sells its first lien on the property to a tax sale purchaser. Bidders must register online at annearundel.marylandtaxsale.com. A final list of tax sale properties is posted on the website before the sale. Maryland is a tax lien state, meaning the owner retains title and can redeem the property.

ftm.office_official: Anne Arundel County Office of Finance, Tax Sale Division
ftm.notes: The delinquent tax roll is typically available in the weeks leading up to the annual tax sale in June. This list identifies properties with unpaid taxes before they are offered at auction. Contact the Tax Sale Division for information on the current delinquent roll.

ftm.office_address: 160 Duke of Gloucester Street, Annapolis, MD 21401
ftm.notes: The City of Annapolis levies its own property tax. A separate delinquent tax list would be maintained by the City's Finance Department. Check the City of Annapolis website or contact their Finance Department for information on their tax sale process and delinquent roll.

ftm.office_official: City of Annapolis, Department of Planning and Zoning, Code Enforcement
ftm.office_address: 160 Duke of Gloucester Street, Annapolis, MD 21401
ftm.notes: The City of Annapolis handles code enforcement within its municipal limits. Information on code violations may be available through their Department of Planning and Zoning. Many cities use online portals for citizen access to code enforcement records; check the City of Annapolis website for such a portal.

ftm.office_official: Anne Arundel County, Department of Inspections and Permits, Code Enforcement Division
ftm.notes: Code violations in unincorporated areas of Anne Arundel County are handled by the Department of Inspections and Permits. Their website provides information on code enforcement. Records may be accessible through a public records request or an online portal if available.

ftm.office_official: Anne Arundel County, Department of Inspections and Permits, Code Enforcement Division
ftm.notes: Information regarding condemned, unsafe structures, or demolition orders would typically fall under the purview of the Code Enforcement Division within the Department of Inspections and Permits. Public records requests may be necessary to obtain specific property lists.

ftm.office_official: District Court of Maryland for Anne Arundel County, Clerk's Office
ftm.office_address: 251 Rowe Blvd, Annapolis, MD 21401 (Annapolis District Court)
ftm.notes: Eviction (Tenant Holding Over/Wrongful Detainer) cases are heard in the District Court. The statewide Case Search portal (casesearch.courts.state.md.us/casesearch/) can be used to search for eviction filings. Searching by plaintiff name (landlord) can identify landlords with multiple filings. The District Court also has a Glen Burnie location (7500 Ritchie Hwy, Glen Burnie, MD 21061, 410-260-1370).

ftm_narrative: Data gaps to know about: SiftMap data (provider data) is low or zero in Anne Arundel County, MD for: Foreclosure notices, Tax sale list. These are proven deal-makers nationally, and nobody can buy them here, so the county pulls below are not a backup, they are the only way in: treat them as priority pulls. Also not in SiftMap here: Eviction filings, Code violations, Divorce filings.
Sources pulled straight from the county the day records publish, 30 to 90 days before paid data. 'Verify locally' means confirm the link before you work it.

read_me.Doors/deal: Live list size divided by the deals that list produced in the window. Lower is better: fewer doors to work per closed deal.
read_me.Lift: County baseline doors/deal divided by the signal's doors/deal. 3.0 means three times sharper than pulling the whole county.
read_me.Baseline: The whole county unfiltered, counted the same way; the denominator every signal is judged against.
read_me.Stack: Records sitting on two distress lists at once. Stacks are distress plus distress; AI is never AND-stacked on distress.
read_me.AI score: DataSift Investor AI likelihood-to-sell score, 0-100, a PARALLEL pull alongside the distress lists.
read_me.score-gated: Live AI-scored supply counts are provisioned per account, so a local doors/deal cannot be computed in this view. The deals and coverage are this county's own data.
read_me.Verify supply: The row tripped the verify rule (v2.1 coverage-aware: verify reasons annotate (churn: doors/deal < 5; small: list < 250) without demoting; only judicial notice lists and churn artifacts (doors/deal < 1) force P3. Volume floors: P1 needs >=2% of county deal flow or >=25 deals, P2 >=1% or >=12 deals): demand is real, treat the efficiency as directional until you price the live list.
read_me.Evidence A / B / C: from this county's own sold deals / cross-market benchmark / single-market anchor (Knox + Blount TN AI measurement)
read_me.Typical gross: Median of AVM value minus purchase price on clean deals: acquisition spread, not net profit.
read_me.Non-disclosure states: Sale prices are not public there, so deal-dollar columns are omitted; doors/deal and lift never use dollars.

ftm_verdicts.src: BOTH the recorder's trustee-sale filings AND the court foreclosure docket (the lender picks the path in this state; run one cycle of both, keep the one that fills)
the county treasurer / tax collector's lien-sale list
the city code-enforcement docket (city-level; often a public records request)
the family / domestic-relations court docket (property sits on the asset schedule)
